name: device-switch-ron
description: Sampling-switch R_on vs input voltage for NMOS / PMOS / transmission gate, 3.3 V devices, over the full PVT matrix.
claim: None yet — device characterization ahead of a ratified spec line (#1). Feeds #10 (sample-switch topology: T-gate vs bootstrapped) and the CDAC settling budget in #8.

ron_n_f00.description: NMOS switch at its best input point (source at ground, no body effect, full gate overdrive). All three PVT axes must move it: process via Vth/mobility, temperature via mobility, supply via overdrive. This is the sensitivity anchor for the whole testbench.

ron_t_max.description: worst-case transmission-gate R_on over the input range — the number #10 budgets settling against. The supply floor matters most: the T-gate mid-range hump grows fast as the supply droops, because both devices lose overdrive at once.

ron_t_flatness.description: R_on(worst input) / R_on(best input) for the transmission gate. A plain T-gate is not flat; how unflat it is at the worst PVT corner is exactly the input to the T-gate vs bootstrapped-switch decision. The bound is deliberately loose — this check exists to catch a broken netlist (flatness < 1 is impossible, a huge value means a branch went open), not to encode a spec.

evidence.data_provenance: simulated — gf180mcu ngspice device models (sm141064.ngspice nfet_03v3 / pfet_03v3 subckts from the fets_mm section, mismatch switch off), over the harness's five MOS process corners. No foundry datasheet or literature value is involved.
notes: R_on is measured as 10 mV / |I| with the switch source held at the input voltage — a small-signal triode resistance at that input, not a large-signal settling average.

Input points track the supply (f * vdd_val, f = 0 .. 1 in sevenths). A fixed 0-3.3 V ladder would place the input 330 mV above the rail at the 2.97 V supply corner, forward-biasing the PMOS source-body junction and measuring a diode instead of a switch. The corollary is a real constraint for #1/#10: a full-scale 0-3.3 V input is not samplable at a drooped 2.97 V supply.
Geometry is pinned at NMOS W = 10 um / PMOS W = 20 um, both L = 0.28 um. R_on scales as ~1/W, so #10 can rescale; the flatness ratio ron_t_flatness is W-independent to first order.
Body connections are single-well: NMOS body to ground, PMOS body to vdd. The body effect is therefore included, and is most of why the NMOS branch degrades toward the top of the input range.
